suites.name: M10r Reproducibility and Branch Label Audit
Branch Signature Dose-Response and Minimal Set

supportedClaims: RecoverFP produces two reproducible Omega outcome families: low (≈1.1) and high (≈2.0–2.7).
A finite-N threshold exists at N≈66: below N≤65, >95% low-branch; at N≥66, high branch accessible.
Branch mixing explains Omega seed variability near the threshold.
Branch split is NOT caused by simple statistics, cluster membership, or generic Kuramoto dynamics.
Branch split is NOT caused by strong pre-RecoverFP predictors or single scalar controls (K_std, λ₁).
Coupling/distance structure separates future branches before Omega itself.
Multi-feature LDA signature on coupling/distance diagnostics classifies branches with 86–100% accuracy.
Signature disruption changes branch outcomes 9–42× more than preserved scores.
High branch is fragile to perturbation; destruction-asymmetric (easier to destroy than create).
Branches form two connected basins with narrow bridge (silhouette 0.32–0.47).
N is the primary regime driver of the stability transition.
Omega seed-stability is regime-dependent; supported at V4.1 regime, weakened at V5.3 regime.
MeanDist seed-variability does not reproduce as claimed in V5.2; V5.2 CV~0.05, not ~0.30.
The V5.2 UncMeanDist=0.30 was an uncertainty budget constant, not a measured CV.
Omega xi-sensitivity is RecoverFP-specific and partly branch-mixing-mediated.
conditionalClaims: All results are at fixed V4.1 baseline (ξ=1.75, K₀=1.20, s=0.10, exp coupling) unless otherwise noted.
Branch counts depend on fixed threshold from N=65 baseline.
Signature accuracy depends on feature set, LDA model, and seed split.
Results are at finite N (60–100); continuum limit not characterized.
Results do not establish physical validity.
Branch signature is conditionally supported as intervention-linked, not proven causal.
hypotheses: The M14 branch signature may correspond to a low-dimensional manifold coordinate.
The bridge between basins may be a topological bottleneck, not a continuous transition.
Branch geometry may reveal whether the split is a genuine bifurcation or a projection artifact.
The N≈66 threshold may generalize to other coupling laws or frequency distributions.
Cross-regime branch maps may reveal whether branch structure is universal or regime-specific.
